tasks.title: Admit turn and budget exhaustion as their own failure categories
tasks.objective: Give the ledger somewhere to record an invocation that never produced a candidate, so a ceiling reached is distinguishable from a candidate rejected.
acceptance_criteria: `store.py` accepts `turn_exhaustion` and `budget_exhaustion` wherever it accepts `review_rejection` and `verification_failure`, in both `record_rejection` and `retry_attempt`, and still rejects an unknown category.

A new category survives the whole path from the ledger event to the evidence a routing policy gate reads, and is then excluded there, so an invocation that produced no candidate cannot be promoted or demoted as if it had. A safelist that silently drops an unknown category before the gate sees it does not satisfy this.
Ledgers recorded before this change remain readable and their existing categories keep their meaning.
Tests cover each new category through both entry points, an unknown category still refused, and a policy gate ignoring the new categories.

tasks.title: Classify an invocation's terminal reason from its result, not its exit code
tasks.objective: Parse an agent invocation's own result before raising on the exit code, so a turn that exhausted its turns or its budget reaches the coordinator as that, rather than as a generic nonzero exit.
acceptance_criteria: The Claude adapter parses the result stream before raising on `outcome.returncode`, and a stream whose result carries `max_turns` or `budget_exhausted` raises an error carrying that classification rather than only `Claude Code execution exited with code 1`.
The Codex adapter's own terminal vocabulary is classified the same way, or its absence is recorded explicitly in the adapter rather than left implicit.
A classified terminal reason reaches the ledger as the matching failure category from the preceding ticket, so the reason is readable from saved state without re-reading raw event files.
A timeout, a malformed stream, a permission denial and an ordinary nonzero exit keep their current behavior and are not reclassified as exhaustion.
Tests drive each terminal reason through a fake agent executable and assert both the raised classification and the recorded category, never invoking a live model.

tasks.title: Enforce a dollar ceiling only where the cost basis is billed
tasks.objective: Distinguish a billed cost from a subscription list-price estimate, and stop terminating an invocation against money that was never charged.
acceptance_criteria: `telemetry.py` records the cost basis a provider reported alongside the amount, so a list-price estimate and a billed charge are distinguishable in saved state rather than sharing `provider_reported_estimate`.
A profile's `max_budget_usd` is passed to an invocation only when the resolved basis is billed; under a list basis the ceiling is not enforced and the reason is recorded rather than silently dropped.
An unknown or absent basis is treated as not billed, so a missing field cannot cause a ceiling to be enforced against an estimate.
Ledgers and invocation records written before this change remain readable, and a run with no `max_budget_usd` configured behaves exactly as it does today.
Tests cover a billed basis enforcing the ceiling, a list basis not enforcing it, an absent basis not enforcing it, and the recorded basis surviving a round trip.
